$comment: Total Gym exercise catalog. See docs/adr/0004 for the copyright position.
Exercise NAMES are unprotectable short phrases (37 C.F.R. 202.1(a)) and the movements
themselves are unprotectable systems or methods (Bikram's Yoga College v. Evolation Yoga,
9th Cir. 2015). What IS protected is Total Gym's photography, illustration, and
instructional prose -- so every 'cue' line here is written from scratch and no artwork is
reproduced.
NOT A TRANSCRIPTION OF THE TRAINING DECK. Total Gym sells a deck of 80 exercise cards, and
no public source enumerates it. This catalog is built from the movements the machine
actually supports, organized under the same categories the deck advertises (chest, back,
shoulders, arms, legs, abs, total body, stretch). Overlap is inevitable and expected -- a
chest press is a chest press -- but the selection here is ours and the card numbering is
not reproduced.
ACCESSORIES ARE A SEPARATE VOCABULARY from what an exercise requires. An exercise names a
capability ('Wing attachment'); the trainee owns a product ('Wing attachment (two-piece)').
Total Gym shipped the wing as one piece and as two, and both do every wing exercise, so an
exercise that named the product would hide pull-ups from half the owners in the world.
accessories[].added is the registry version the accessory first appeared in. A trainee who
ticked their equipment before it existed answered a shorter question than the one being
asked now, and silence is not a 'no' -- anything newer than the version they answered shows
its exercises until they say otherwise. See ExerciseCatalog.resolveOwned.
category    : grouping for the exercise picker. Presentation only.
kind        : 'strength' counts toward weekly training volume; 'stretch' does not. Without
this, adding stretches would silently inflate every muscle's set count and
make the coach's volume advice wrong (docs/adr/0010).
usesPulley  : true when the movement routes through the cable, which halves the load.
setup       : how the trainee is arranged on the machine -- position, which end of the rail
they face ('tower' is the pulley end), and what is in their hands. Drives both
the setup instructions and the session ordering, because two movements that
share a setup can be done back to back without rebuilding the machine.
alsoFacing names a second direction the movement works at, where one exists --
a curl is fine either way round. That is not a footnote: it lets a curl sit in
a block of pressing without anybody turning around.
peakTension : where in the range the muscle is most loaded -- 'lengthened', 'even', or
'shortened'. Loaded work at long muscle lengths grows a muscle more than the
same sets through a shortened range, and a cable machine holds tension at the
bottom of a fly where a dumbbell goes slack, so a hypertrophy program built on
this machine should lean on it (docs/adr/0010). A JUDGMENT about mechanics, in
the same class as bodyFraction: it changes which exercise gets suggested first,
never a recorded number.
bodyFraction: share of bodyweight actually riding the glideboard. Supine work is ~1.0;
seated and kneeling positions put less of the trainee on the board.
THESE ARE ESTIMATES, not measurements -- see the open item in docs/adr/README.
Getting them wrong shifts absolute load but not progression, because every
set for an exercise uses the same figure.
muscles     : fraction 1.0 = prime mover, 0.5 = meaningful secondary involvement.
Fractional accounting matters because Total Gym work is almost all compound;
see docs/adr/0010.

accessories.name: Wing attachment (two-piece)
accessories.note: Ships with most machines -- the two bars that bolt on either side at the top.

accessories.name: Wing attachment (one-piece)
accessories.note: The single-bar version of the same thing. Either one does every wing exercise.

accessories.name: Weighted vest
accessories.note: Adds load to any exercise. Discounted by the incline -- 10 lb at level 8 is about 3 lb.

accessories.name: Weight bar
accessories.note: Bolts to the glideboard, so its weight is not discounted the way a vest is.

exercises.name: Chest Press
exercises.cue: Handles level with your chest, elbows tucked, press until your arms are straight.

exercises.name: Chest Fly
exercises.cue: Arms wide with elbows softly bent, sweep the handles together in front of your chest.

exercises.name: Incline Chest Fly
exercises.cue: Same sweep as a chest fly, set a notch or two higher so the top of the chest takes more of it.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Chest Press
exercises.cue: Press one handle at a time. Keep both hips flat on the board so you don't twist into it.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Chest Press
exercises.cue: Press with your elbows tucked close to your ribs. Most of the work moves to the triceps.

exercises.name: Chest Crossover
exercises.cue: Fly the handles together and let your hands cross past each other at the top.

exercises.name: Pullover
exercises.cue: Arms straight overhead, pull the handles down over your chest in a wide arc.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.cue: Face down with your head lower than your feet, hands on the bars, press the board away.

exercises.name: Shaper Bar Chest Press
exercises.cue: Press with the shaper bars in a neutral grip. Easier on the shoulders than a flat grip.

exercises.name: Chest Dip
exercises.cue: On the dip bars with your chest leaning forward, lower until you feel a stretch and press back up.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Reach overhead and pull the handles down past your shoulders, leading with your elbows.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pulldown
exercises.cue: A pulldown with your hands set wide. Pull your elbows down and out to the sides.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Pulldown
exercises.cue: Pull down with your palms facing you. The biceps get a full share of this one.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.cue: Keep your arms straight and sweep the handles from overhead down to your hips.

exercises.name: Seated Row
exercises.cue: Sit upright, pull the handles to your waist and squeeze your shoulder blades together.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Row
exercises.cue: Row with your hands wide and your elbows flared out, finishing at the ribs.

exercises.name: High Row
exercises.cue: Row towards your collarbones with your elbows high. Upper back and rear shoulders.

exercises.name: Low Row
exercises.cue: Row low and tight to your body, finishing at the hips with elbows brushing your sides.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Row
exercises.cue: Row one handle at a time. Resist the pull to rotate; that is the core's job here.

exercises.name: Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Arms out in front, sweep them wide and back. Small movement, rear shoulders and upper back.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Grip the wing bars overhead and pull your chest towards them. The incline sets how hard it is.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.cue: Pull-up with your palms facing you, which brings the biceps in properly.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Hands at the far ends of the wing, pull up leading with your elbows out to the sides.

exercises.name: Shaper Bar Row
exercises.cue: Row with the shaper bars in a neutral grip, palms facing each other, elbows past your ribs.

exercises.name: Rope Face Pull
exercises.cue: Pull the rope towards your forehead, splitting the ends apart as your elbows come back.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press
exercises.cue: Sit upright, handles at shoulder height, press straight overhead.

exercises.name: Front Raise
exercises.cue: Arms straight, raise the handles in front of you to about eye level.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Arms straight, raise the handles out to the sides until they're level with your shoulders.

exercises.name: Scaption Raise
exercises.cue: Raise the handles halfway between straight ahead and straight out. Kinder on the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.cue: Pull the handles up along your body to chest height, elbows leading and above your wrists.

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrug
exercises.cue: Arms straight, lift your shoulders towards your ears without bending your elbows.

exercises.name: External Rotation
exercises.cue: Elbow tucked at your side and bent, rotate your forearm outwards. Light loads, this is rotator cuff work.

exercises.name: Internal Rotation
exercises.cue: Elbow tucked and bent, rotate your forearm across your body. Light loads.

exercises.name: Biceps Curl
exercises.cue: Sit upright, elbows fixed at your sides, curl the handles up to your shoulders.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Curl with your palms facing each other the whole way, like holding a hammer.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
exercises.cue: Curl with your palms facing down. Harder than it looks, and it hits the forearms.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Curl
exercises.cue: Curl with your hands set wide and elbows out slightly.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.cue: One arm, elbow braced against your inner thigh, curl slowly and don't swing.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Curl
exercises.cue: Curl one handle at a time and keep your shoulders square as you do it.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Curl
exercises.cue: Lie back with the cables coming from above your head and curl towards your forehead, elbows still.

exercises.name: Rope Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Curl the rope with your palms facing each other and pull the ends apart at the top.

exercises.name: Shaper Bar Curl
exercises.cue: Curl the shaper bars with your elbows pinned. The grip angle takes the strain off your wrists.

exercises.name: Triceps Extension
exercises.cue: Elbows high and still, straighten your arms against the cable.

exercises.name: Triceps Pushdown
exercises.cue: Elbows pinned to your sides, push the handles down until your arms lock out.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.cue: Lie back with the handles behind your head, straighten your arms without moving your elbows.

exercises.name: Triceps Kickback
exercises.cue: Upper arm still and parallel to the board, straighten your elbow behind you.

exercises.name: Triceps Dip
exercises.cue: Hands on the bars behind you, lower until your elbows are bent, then press back up.

exercises.name: Upright Dip
exercises.cue: On the dip bars with your torso upright and elbows tracking straight back. Triceps take it.

exercises.name: Rope Pushdown
exercises.cue: Elbows at your sides, push the rope down and spread the ends apart as your arms lock out.

exercises.name: Overhead Rope Extension
exercises.cue: Rope behind your head, elbows high and still, straighten your arms and split the ends.

exercises.name: Squat
exercises.cue: Feet flat on the squat stand, lower until your knees are bent, then drive the board back up.

exercises.name: Wide-Stance Squat
exercises.cue: Squat with your feet wide and toes turned out. More glute and inner thigh.

exercises.name: Narrow-Stance Squat
exercises.cue: Squat with your feet close together. The quads take most of it.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Squat
exercises.cue: One foot on the stand, the other tucked away. Keep your knee tracking over your toes.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.cue: One foot high on the stand and one low, lower and drive back up without shifting your weight.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.cue: Squat down and push off hard enough that your feet leave the stand. Land soft.

exercises.name: Hip Bridge
exercises.cue: Feet on the stand, drive your hips up until your body is a straight line, then lower.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Balls of your feet on the edge of the stand, press up onto your toes and lower slowly.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.cue: One foot on the edge of the stand, press up onto your toes and lower under control.

exercises.name: Toe Press
exercises.cue: Legs almost straight, push the board using only your ankles.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction
exercises.cue: Lie on your side and press the board away with the top leg, opening the hip.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction
exercises.cue: Lie on your side and press with the bottom leg, drawing it in towards the midline.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Lift
exercises.cue: On your side, lift the top leg against the incline. Small, controlled, no swinging.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curl
exercises.cue: Face down with the straps on your ankles, bend your knees to draw your heels towards you.

exercises.name: Wing Hamstring Curl
exercises.cue: Face down with your heels hooked on the wing, bend your knees to pull the board up the rail.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.cue: Seated with the straps on your ankles, straighten your knees against the cable.

exercises.name: Glute Kickback
exercises.cue: Strap on one ankle, push that leg back and up without arching your lower back.

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.cue: Lie back on the board and curl your ribs towards your hips. Short range, no pulling on your neck.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.cue: Hold the handles by your head and crunch down against the cable.

exercises.name: Oblique Crunch
exercises.cue: Crunch up and across, taking one shoulder towards the opposite hip.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.cue: Knees bent, curl your hips up off the board. The legs stay passive.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.cue: Alternate elbow to opposite knee, extending the other leg as you go.

exercises.name: Knee Tuck
exercises.cue: Face down in a plank on the board, draw both knees up towards your chest.

exercises.name: Pike
exercises.cue: From the same plank, keep your legs straight and lift your hips towards the ceiling.

exercises.name: Plank Hold
exercises.cue: Forearms on the board, body in a straight line, and hold. Count time, not reps.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.cue: One forearm down, hips stacked and lifted. Hold, then swap sides.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
exercises.cue: Hold the wing overhead and draw your knees up towards your chest.

exercises.name: AbCrunch Curl-Up
exercises.cue: Head towards the top, arms hooked over the pads, curl your ribs down and let the board follow.

exercises.name: AbCrunch Oblique Twist
exercises.cue: Same curl-up, but drive one shoulder across towards the opposite hip. Alternate sides.

exercises.name: Leg Pull
exercises.cue: Feet in the accessory, pull your legs down and in against the cable.

exercises.name: Torso Rotation
exercises.cue: Arms out in front, rotate your ribcage away from the cable and return slowly.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchop
exercises.cue: Pull the handle diagonally across your body, high to low, turning through the trunk.

exercises.name: Pullover to Press
exercises.cue: Pull over from overhead, then press straight up from your chest. One rep is both halves.

exercises.name: Row to Curl
exercises.cue: Row to your waist, then curl the handles up to your shoulders before lowering.

exercises.name: Press to Fly
exercises.cue: Press up, then open your arms wide and sweep them back together.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.cue: Plank on the board, drive one knee up at a time at a steady pace.

exercises.name: Board Burpee
exercises.cue: Tuck your knees in, press the board out to a plank, then pull back and drive out through your feet.

exercises.name: Sprinter Start
exercises.cue: One foot loaded on the stand, drive it out explosively and return under control.

exercises.name: Pilates Footwork
exercises.cue: Toes on the bar, heels lifted, press the board away and return slowly under control.

exercises.name: Pilates Frog
exercises.cue: Heels together and knees open, press out until your legs are straight, then fold back in.

exercises.name: Pilates Leg Circle
exercises.cue: Legs straight against the bar, trace a slow circle without letting your hips rock.

exercises.name: Pilates Scooter
exercises.cue: One foot on the bar and one leg free, push the board away with the working leg only.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.cue: Lie back, straighten one leg towards the ceiling and draw it gently in. Hold and breathe.

exercises.name: Quad Stretch
exercises.cue: Kneel on the board and ease your hips forward until you feel the front of the thigh open.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.cue: Half-kneeling, let the incline carry your hips forward. Front of the hip, not the lower back.

exercises.name: Glute Stretch
exercises.cue: Ankle crossed over the opposite knee, draw both legs in towards your chest.

exercises.name: Inner Thigh Stretch
exercises.cue: Feet wide on the stand, let your knees ease apart and hold where it's comfortable.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch
exercises.cue: Ball of one foot on the edge of the stand, let the heel drop and hold.

exercises.name: Chest Stretch
exercises.cue: Arms wide with the handles, let them draw your chest open. Stop well short of pain.

exercises.name: Lat Stretch
exercises.cue: Reach overhead, hold the handles and let your ribs lengthen away from your hips.

exercises.name: Shoulder Stretch
exercises.cue: One arm across your body, use the other to draw it in until the back of the shoulder opens.

exercises.name: Spinal Twist
exercises.cue: Lie back, drop both knees to one side and keep both shoulders on the board.
